result:
The analysis is done, but no fix has landed and the arm is not registered. The three files the fix needs are held by other lanes, so the code exists only as a patch in PR #306, which is now marked ready. Preflight passes; CI is running on the pushed head.

**1. The rule.** I re-derived it myself by testing 112 candidate rule combinations against all 64 golden half-swatches, in all four channels. PR #176 checked 32 halves, red channel only, and the scorer also counts alpha.
- **Rule:** memory holds `(X<<7)|A7`. The texture unit returns that byte as-is. The blend unit reads the 7-bit alpha stretched back to 8 bits. That stretch gives exactly the same result as `round(v*255/127)` on all 128 values, so the existing clear path already stores the right byte.
- **The 1,772 px it can't reproduce:** the `XA_*_Add_SrcA_DstA` pair, 886 structural each. Hardware rounds alpha to 7 bits after blending, and fixed-function blending can't do that.

**2. The design.** My model of today's behaviour reproduces the device capture on all 64 halves, on both the Nova (851650a) and Thor (a7b9d28) runs.
- **Read side:** returning `(X<<7)|(h>>1)` at the texture fetch takes the four DstAlpha captures from 229,376 structural px to **0**. It leaves 65,536 px that are off by one.
- **Write side:** stretching alpha on unblended writes is worth only those off-by-one px. I left it out so an arm can tell which change moved what.
- **Hunks** (`docs/lanes/x1a7271/x1a7-read-side.diff`, applies cleanly to master 724a0dd868; **not compiled**, because this host has no desktop build tree):

| file | holder | hunk |
|---|---|---|
| `glsl/psh.h` | unclaimed (`[free]`) | a per-stage uniform, `texX1A7[4]` |
| `glsl/psh.c` | lane.wbufdepth24 (#268) | the alpha transform after each texture fetch, plus uniform staging |
| `vk/texture.c` | lane.texvol283 (#289) | sets the mode when the sampled surface is X1A7 |

- **`vk/draw.c`:** not needed, despite the brief naming it.

**3. Priced offline.**

| capture | differing now | predicted |
|---|---:|---:|
| four DstAlpha | 294,912 | 65,536 (0 structural) |
| `Clear/SCF_X1A7R8G8B8_{Z,O}` | 131,040 | 0 |
| `Fmt_X1A7R8G8B8_Z` | 32,743 | improves (GL measured the same rule at 32,774 → 6,311) |
| `Fmt_X1A7R8G8B8_O` | 16,383 | **worse by at least 58,754** |

The `Fmt_X1A7R8G8B8_O` loss comes from its background. The test clears that memory with a CPU memset, the GPU never draws there, and hardware reads it back as 0x00. The new rule forces the pad bit on and reads 0x80. GL measured 59,025 px for the same rule.
- **Per-pixel fix:** ruled out, because blended writes leave the low bit I'd need arbitrary.
- **Per-surface gate:** might work, but it needs a device probe and `vk/surface.c`, which lane.remote holds.

**4. The arm.** I didn't register it, because its patched build would need commits to the held files. The legs are written out in NOTES section 4, ready to register:
- **must_move:** the four DstAlpha captures and the Clear pair.
- **declared regression:** `Fmt_X1A7R8G8B8_O`.
- **must_not_move:** each of the other formats, with the change that would move it.

I've reported this on #271.
